John Ternus officially takes over as Apple's CEO today, and he has revealed some of his key focus areas on his new profile page on the Apple website, as spotted by Myke Hurley.

John Ternus's new Apple profile reveals his priorities on his first day as CEO

Apple updated its leadership page today to reflect John Ternus's new title of CEO.

In addition to the leadership page update, Ternus's official bio has also been refreshed and expanded.

As Myke Hurley noted over at The Enthusiast, the new bio centres around Ternus's time at Apple and the work he cares deeply about, highlighting three key narratives. Two of those narratives are built around newly added content.

The bio reuses some of the previous content, but includes one entirely new paragraph, which is quoted below. The content comes from the Apple website:

This is the only completely new paragraph. The rest of the bio is either identical to before or has slightly tweaked wording, but the core messaging has not changed.

The new paragraph makes up nearly half of the entire bio, and the bio as a whole is relatively short.

So this paragraph makes it very clear what Ternus values and wants to emphasise as he steps into the CEO role.

In summary, Ternus cares about the "reliability and durability" of hardware, as well as "innovation in materials and hardware design," with the goal of reducing carbon footprints and extending the lifespan of products.

We've seen Tim Cook place a heavy emphasis on reducing Apple's carbon footprint. Ternus is clearly signalling that under his leadership, that direction will continue. But the passage also emphasises that Ternus is an innovator in hardware design, focused on creating products that will last for years.

What do you think of John Ternus's new CEO bio? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
